key_insight: Applying Evolutionary Strategies (ES) as a gradient-free method for post-deployment learning in LLMs leads to severe catastrophic forgetting — ES reduces memory needs but tends to erase previously learned capabilities.
problem_solved: Investigates whether ES can serve as a memory-efficient alternative to gradient-based continual learning for large language models, and exposes its failure modes when deployed for continual adaptation.
method: Implement ES-based continual update loop for LLMs (population-based perturbations and black-box evaluation) as a gradient-free training path.
Empirically compare ES vs gradient-based baselines on multi-task / sequential learning benchmarks, measuring performance retention, forgetting metrics, and memory footprint.
Analyze failure modes: quantify task-wise performance decay, representational drift, and identify scenarios where ES exacerbates forgetting.
impact: Practitioners should not assume gradient-free ES avoids continual-learning pitfalls—ES can be highly memory-efficient but induces catastrophic forgetting unless paired with mitigation (replay, regularization, or hybrid approaches). This finding redirects research toward robust ES-compatible continual-learning strategies.
visual_elements: Timeline chart showing model accuracy per task over sequential updates: steep drop when using ES (visualizes catastrophic forgetting).
Bar chart comparing memory footprint and peak performance of ES vs gradient-based continual learning.
Schematic of ES update loop (population → evaluate → select/mutate) contrasted with gradient descent loop for clarity.
Heatmap of task performance across tasks and checkpoints to show representational drift and selective forgetting.
paper_title: Evolutionary Strategies lead to Catastrophic Forgetting in LLMs
paper_authors: Immanuel Abdi, Akshat Gupta, Micah Mok, Alexander Lu, Nicholas Lee
